questions.prompt: Abstraction in C# is primarily provided by:
questions.explanation: Abstract classes and interfaces define contracts without full implementation.

questions.prompt: An abstract method in an abstract class:
options: Has no body and must be overridden
questions.explanation: Abstract methods declare a signature only.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank to declare an abstract class with an abstract method
blanks: public abstract class Shape { public abstract double Area(); }

questions.prompt: You cannot instantiate an abstract class because:
options: It may have unimplemented abstract members
questions.explanation: Abstract members must be implemented by a concrete subclass.

questions.prompt: Create abstract class Animal { public abstract string Sound(); } and class Cow:Animal { public override string Sound(){return "Moo";} }, print new Cow().Sound()
Compared to interfaces, abstract classes can also provide:
questions.explanation: Abstract classes can hold fields and concrete methods.

questions.prompt: Arrange an abstract base and concrete derived type
items: abstract class Vehicle { public abstract void Start(); }

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank to require a subclass to implement a property
The Dependency Inversion Principle encourages depending on:
questions.explanation: High-level modules should depend on abstractions.

questions.prompt: Create abstract class Calculator { public abstract int Compute(int a,int b); } and class Add:Calculator { public override int Compute(int a,int b){return a+b;} }, print new Add().Compute(3,7)
